{"self_assessment": "Impact
Our table drew a fish, which reads clearly from the outline alone: a big body, a distinct tail fin, and a start that reached nearly all the standing dominoes. I laid the bottom arc and carried it all the way to the crossing, which was one of the two long body lines. I also worked on the lower edge of the tail fin and the bottom corner joint. I can't claim the idea or the sketch, since Maya proposed the fish and Leo drew the pad. A few spare dominoes near the crossing stayed pale, but they shouldn't show in the picture.

Execution
My bottom arc was done early and connected. I spotted the gap at the bottom corner of the tail and worked on the lower edge's joint. Where I was less sharp: I announced a nudge at the crossing domino, then reversed myself and said it was fine, and Leo's inspection showed it really was off. His bridge ended up fixing it. I should have trusted my own close look instead of talking myself out of it. I also asked Priya about the lower edge when I could have just checked the table.

Collaboration
I offered to take the far half of the top arc and the vertical bar, accepted Leo's call to keep the arc himself, and stayed out of his way. I kept my updates specific, with a point at the spot, and kept my hands off the crossing while Leo worked. I probably added to the chatter near the end with repeated "hands off" agreements.

Leadership
I took charge of coordinating the tail: who had which edge, and where the joints were. I didn't try to override Leo's ownership of the sketch and the top arc, which kept the table calm. My lapse was the flip-flop at the crossing, which cost a few minutes. Next time I'd flag a suspected break once, verify it, and either fix it or hand it clearly to someone."}
